additions.reason: Free choice (בחירה) is the sole subject of this Torah. The Rebbe asserts it plainly and emphatically as an ever-present capacity belonging to every person. It is the positive teaching — the liberating truth that a person is never trapped by his habits. בחירה is the dominant conceptual node of this Torah.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁהַבְּחִירָה הִיא בְּיַד הָאָדָם בִּפְשִׁיטוּת, אִם רוֹצֶה עוֹשֶׂה, וְאִם אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה אֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה

additions.reason: Will/desire (רצון) is the operative mechanism of free choice as defined by the Rebbe. The definition of בחירה is precisely the power of the will — 'if he wants, he does; if he does not want, he does not do.' Will is not a separate concept from free choice here but its very content: what it means to have free choice is to have a functional will.
additions.source_quote: אִם רוֹצֶה עוֹשֶׂה, וְאִם אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה אֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה

additions.reason: Habit and ingrained ways of conduct (מורגלים במעשיהם ובדרכיהם מנעוריהם) are the source of the false perception that free choice does not exist. They form the negative counterpart — the thing that fools a person into thinking he is trapped. This is the evil mirror to בחירה: not a physical evil but the illusion that blocks the person from exercising his true freedom.
additions.source_quote: מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהֵם מֻרְגָּלִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם וּבְדַרְכֵיהֶם מִנְּעוּרֵיהֶם מְאֹד, עַל־כֵּן נִדְמֶה לָהֶם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם בְּחִירָה

additions.reason: The false perception (נדמה להם — 'it seems to them') is the explicit mental error the Torah identifies and corrects. It is the illusion that one has no free choice. This is distinct from habit itself — it is the cognitive distortion produced by habit. Together with הרגל, it forms the evil/obstacle side of the Torah: the two components of the trap (the habit + the false belief it generates).
additions.source_quote: עַל־כֵּן נִדְמֶה לָהֶם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם בְּחִירָה, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְאֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לְשַׁנּוֹת מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם

analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: LM2 Torah 110 is a three-sentence record of an oral teaching — entirely the Rebbe's plain verbal response to a question about the nature of free choice. The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear anywhere in the text. The Rebbe does not draw conceptual equivalences; he makes a direct philosophical-practical declaration: free choice is real and always operative. The Torah identifies one positive reality (בחירה/רצון — the freedom and will that is always present) and one obstacle-structure (הרגל + the false perception it generates). These map naturally onto a good/evil pair. Because this Torah contains no bechina declarations whatsoever, the additions above represent the full conceptual structure of the Torah as derived from close reading, not from explicit bechina language. The two thematic domains — (1) the reality of free choice and will, and (2) the illusion created by habituated behavior — form a clean good/evil mirror. The Rebbe's statement 'וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה עוֹשֶׂה' at the Torah's closing is a deliberate restatement that emphasizes the permanence and simplicity of the freedom.
analysis_notes.reason_no_bechina_additions: The source text contains zero bechina declarations. There is no instance of 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' or any equivalent ontological equating language. The teaching is a brief, plain, practical statement. The concepts are discussed assertively, not as parallel aspects of a shared nature. Therefore all additions are derived from thematic/conceptual reading rather than explicit bechina constructions.
